questions.question: Which of the following oceans in the smallest in area
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**the Arctic**__. 

__
 
• **The Arctic Ocean is the smallest ocean basin in the world__,** with a gross area of** 14 million square kilometres (5.4 million square miles)**. 
 
• It is **1.5 times the size of the United States**, with a gross area of around 14 million square kilometres (5.4 million square miles). 
 
• The Arctic Ocean is, perhaps the most remote and least explored of all the main ocean basins of the World. 
 
• Owing to year-round ice cover, the** deepest areas of the Arctic Ocean** (5,441 metres; 17,850 feet), known as the Canada Basin, are especially remote and unexplored. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

 
• The Arctic Ocean is the smallest of the five main oceans in the world and the shallowest. It is also regarded as the coldest of all oceans. 
 
• **The International Hydrographic Organisation (IHO)** acknowledges it as an ocean, although it is called the Arctic Mediterranean Sea by some oceanographers. 
 
• In the centre of the Northern Hemisphere, the Arctic Ocean contains the North Pole area, which stretches south to around 60° N. 
 
• Eurasia and North America circle the Arctic Ocean, and the boundaries meet topographic features; on the Pacific side, the Bering Strait, and on the Atlantic side, the Greenland Scotland Range.

questions.question: Which British ruler introduced the Police Administration in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option __1__ i.e. __**Lord Cornwallis**__.

__
 
• In **pre-colonial India**, the governments, under the Mughals and other native states, were autocratic in nature, and **lacked a separate or formal police system**. However, there have been watch guards since time immemorial protecting villages at night.
 
• Later, **under the Mughal rule** there were the ***faujdars*** who helped in maintaining law and order, ***amils*** who were basically revenue collectors but had to contend with rebels, if any and the ***kotwal*** was responsible for maintenance of law and order in the cities.
 
• Even **during the dual rule** in Bengal, Bihar and Orissa **between 1765 and 1772** the **zamindars were expected** to maintain the staff including ***thanedars*** for law and order duties and for maintaining peace, as well as dealing with crime and criminals but very often, the zamidars neglected their duties and were even said to have colluded with dacoits and shared their loot.
 
• **In 1770**, the institution of the ***faujdar* and *amils* were abolished**.
 
• However, **in 1774, Warren Hastings** **restored the institution of *faujdars*** and asked the zamindars to assist them in suppression of dacoits, violence and disorder.
 
• **In 1775, *faujdar thanas* were established** in the major towns of large districts and were assisted by several smaller police stations.
 
• **In 1791 Lord Cornwallis__ (Governor-General, 1786-1793) organised a regular police force to maintain law and order** by going back to and modernising the old Indian system of thanas (circles) in a district under a daroga (an Indian) and a superintendent of police (SP) at the head of a district & relieved the zamindars of their police duties.
 
• **Lord Bentinck (Governor-General, 1828-1835)** abolished the office of the SP.
 
 
• The collector/magistrate was now to head the police force in his jurisdiction and the commissioner in each division was to act as the SP.
 
• This arrangement resulted in a badly organised police force, putting a heavy burden on the collector/magistrate.
 
• Presidency towns were the first to have the duties of collector/magistrate separated.

questions.question: Which of the following combinations of shortcut keys and functions is correctly matched?

options.text: Ctrl + Tab – Copies the selected text
Ctrl + C – Copies content to the clipboard
Ctrl + F – Switches between open tabs
Ctrl + V – Finds a specific word in the document

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ctrl + C – Copies content to the clipboard**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Ctrl + C – Copies content to the clipboard:** This is the standard shortcut used to copy text, images, or other content to the clipboard. Once copied, the content can be pasted elsewhere using the **Ctrl + V** command. *Hence, this statement is correct.*
 
• **Ctrl + Tab – Copies the selected text:** This shortcut is used to switch between open tabs in browsers or applications, not for copying text. *Hence, this statement is incorrect.*
 
• **Ctrl + F – Switches between open tabs:** This shortcut is primarily used to open the "Find" dialog to search for specific words or phrases within a document or webpage. It does not switch between tabs. *Hence, this statement is incorrect.*
 
• **Ctrl + V – Finds a specific word in the document:** This shortcut is used to paste the content from the clipboard. It does not perform the "Find" function. *Hence, this statement is incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Clipboard Functionality:**

 
 
• The clipboard temporarily stores the copied content (text, images, files) until it is pasted elsewhere.
 
• It is an essential feature of operating systems and helps in transferring data efficiently between applications.
 
 
 
• **Common Keyboard Shortcuts:**
 
 
• **Ctrl + X:** Cuts the selected content and moves it to the clipboard.
 
• **Ctrl + Z:** Undoes the last action performed in most applications.
 
• **Ctrl + Y:** Redoes the last undone action.

questions.question: How can you permanently delete a file in MS Windows so that it DOES NOT go to the Recycle Bin?

options.text: Right-click on the file and press 'Shift + Delete'
Right-click on the file and Press Ctrl + D
Drag the file to the Recycle Bin
Right-click on the file and select 'Delete'

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Right-click on the file and press 'Shift + Delete'**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Shift + Delete** is a shortcut in **Microsoft Windows** that permanently deletes a file without sending it to the **Recycle Bin**. This ensures that the file is removed immediately from the system.
 
• When you use this shortcut, the file bypasses the **Recycle Bin**, and the system marks the space occupied by the file as available for new data. *Hence, the statement is correct.*
 
• Using **Ctrl + D** only moves the file to the Recycle Bin instead of permanently deleting it. *Hence, the statement is incorrect.*
 
• Dragging the file to the Recycle Bin is another method of deleting a file, but the file is not permanently deleted as it remains in the Recycle Bin until it is manually emptied. *Hence, the statement is incorrect.*
 
• Right-clicking on the file and selecting "Delete" will also move the file to the Recycle Bin and not permanently delete it. *Hence, the statement is incorrect.*
 
• The **Shift + Delete** method is commonly used when users want to remove sensitive or unnecessary files without the need for additional confirmation from the Recycle Bin.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Key Characteristics of File Deletion Methods:**

 
 
• **Shift + Delete**: Permanently deletes the file, bypassing the **Recycle Bin**. Once deleted, recovering the file may require specialized recovery tools.
 
• **Ctrl + D**: Moves the file to the **Recycle Bin**, allowing the user to restore it if needed.
 
• Dragging the file to the Recycle Bin allows for temporary deletion. The file is not permanently removed until the Recycle Bin is emptied.
 
• Right-click + Delete: Similar to dragging to the Recycle Bin, this only removes the file temporarily unless the Recycle Bin is cleared.
 
 
 
• **Recovering Deleted Files:**
 
 
• Files deleted using **Shift + Delete** are not easily recoverable through standard methods, as they bypass the Recycle Bin. Specialized software like **Recuva** or **EaseUS Data Recovery** is required for recovery.
 
• Files in the **Recycle Bin** can be restored by right-clicking on the file and selecting **Restore**. This places the file back in its original location.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Permanent Deletion:**
 
 
• Permanent deletion is often used for **sensitive data** that users want to remove entirely, such as financial records, personal information, or outdated files.
 
• **Organizations** dealing with sensitive data often rely on permanent deletion methods to ensure compliance with **data protection laws**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Storage and Deletion:**

 
 
• Files are not immediately erased from storage devices when deleted. Instead, the system marks the space as available for new data. This is true for both **Recycle Bin** deletion and **Shift + Delete** deletion.
 
• Specialized software can sometimes recover "permanently" deleted files by analyzing unallocated space on the storage device.
 
 
 
• **Best Practices for Deletion:**
 
 
• Always double-check the file before using **Shift + Delete**, as recovering it later may be difficult or costly.
 
• For highly sensitive information, consider using **data shredding tools** like **Eraser** or **Secure Delete** to ensure complete and irreversible removal.

questions.question: Which keyboard shortcut allows you to select multiple specific files or folders at once?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ctrl + Click**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ctrl + Click** shortcut allows users to select multiple specific files or folders. This is useful when the files are not adjacent to each other and need to be selected individually.
 
• Using **Ctrl + Click** ensures that the selection is additive, meaning that each additional click adds to the already selected items without deselecting others. *Hence, the statement is correct.*
 
• **Tab + Click** is not used for selecting multiple files; it is typically used for navigation between fields or elements in applications. *Hence, this statement is incorrect.*
 
• **Alt + Click** is not a standard shortcut for selecting multiple files; it is often used for specific actions in software (e.g., selecting objects in design software). *Hence, this statement is incorrect.*
 
• **Shift + Click** allows users to select a range of files that are adjacent to each other. However, it is not suitable for selecting non-adjacent files. *Hence, this statement is correct in a different context.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Functionality of Ctrl + Click:**

 
 
• The **Ctrl key**, when held down, allows users to make multiple selections without overriding previous selections.
 
• It is commonly used in **Windows File Explorer** or macOS Finder to select multiple files or folders that are spread across different positions.
 
 
 
• **Shift + Click Usage:**
 
 
• While **Shift + Click** is used to select a range of items, it is limited to selecting items that are adjacent to each other.
 
• For example, if you click the first file, hold **Shift**, and click the last file, all files in between will be selected.
 
 
 
• **Tab Key Usage:**
 
 
• **Tab + Click** is not a valid shortcut for file selection. The **Tab key** is primarily used for navigation between fields or interactive elements.
 
• For example, pressing **Tab** allows users to move to the next field in a form or navigate through buttons and menus.
 
 
 
• **Alt Key Usage:**
 
 
• The **Alt key** is generally used for accessing menus and shortcuts specific to particular software, not for file selection.
 
• In some applications like graphic design software, **Alt + Click** allows advanced selection techniques, but it does not apply to regular file selection.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Advantages of Ctrl + Click:**

 
 
• It enables users to select specific items without affecting the selection of others, making it flexible and efficient.
 
• This shortcut is particularly useful when working with large datasets or organizing files.
 
 
 
• **Applications in Operating Systems:**
 
 
• **Windows OS:** The **Ctrl key** is widely used for multiple selections in File Explorer and other applications.
 
• **macOS:** The equivalent shortcut in macOS is **Command + Click**, serving the same purpose for selecting multiple files.
